title: From Packets to Playback: probability, information and renormalisation in a live stream
summary: Choose the bitrate of the next segment of a live football stream (4K, 1080p, 720p or 480p) from the buffer, live delay, recent throughput, variability, packet loss, persistence and tail behaviour, with the stall probability P(T > B), segment time and live delay behind a schematic utility U(R) = Q(R) − αP(T > B | R) − βL. Show why unfolds Euclidean field-theory notation as a language for probability and information: Gaussian and heavy-tailed candidate models, an effective action whose couplings each have a probability meaning, sources with Z[J] and W[J] = log Z[J], a probability–QFT–information dictionary, a UV-to-IR resolution control that coarse-grains synthetic packet data, running couplings that separate exact aggregation from a truncated projection, relevant and irrelevant perturbations, the central limit theorem as an RG fixed point against a heavy-tail stable law, an information bottleneck compared with RG, and rate–distortion. Live football, movie and video-call presets, a drawn football scene that degrades and stalls, optional Feynman diagrams and a translation challenge. Every trace is synthetic and seeded. Save the decision as a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline, from file:// and in an iframe.
